summary.intent: Assess and plan Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness), audit and reconcile stale/pending todos against Phases 70/70.1/71, then drop everything to fix a live CI outage across web-e2e, desktop-e2e, and sdk-e2e before resuming and executing Phase 72 planning through wave-based implementation.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated Phase 72/73 source-todo lists; diagnosed and shipped fixes for three independent CI regressions (web-e2e IndexedDB floor-store drift, desktop-e2e FUSE seq-1 equivocation, sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency flake) plus web-e2e flakiness across 4 more tests, merging PR #601 and #600 to green main; then planned and executed Phase 72 through Wave 5 of 6 (8 of 10 plans landed, all green) with a new CI-typecheck-drift todo captured for a final hardening plan.

repo: This repo closes todos by deleting them from pending/ and moving to completed/ (via git mv) rather than a separate resolved/ folder — resolved/ is unused/empty
GSD phase source-todo lists live in .planning/ROADMAP.md per-phase sections and must be kept in sync with .planning/todos/{pending,completed}/

ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR checks never exercise it, so branches must be dispatched manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on workflows predating that input) to get pre-merge e2e signal

Playwright web-e2e ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI (process.env.CI) — local runs use the caller's raw (often 15-30s) timeout, causing IPNS-gated-mutation tests to flake locally even when they'd pass in CI; running with CI=1 locally also flips webServer.reuseExistingServer to false and fights an already-running stack

Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring its 8 source todos from pending/, and left three separate pieces of test/fixture drift unaddressed: a stale desktop-e2e .mts driver using pre-rename DTO field names, an sdk-e2e assertion that didn't account for its own new idempotency behavior, and it exposed a latent FUSE seq-1 equivocation bug

Share DTO fields were renamed in Phase 71: readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, writeDescriptorRef→encryptedWriteKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName; desktop-e2e .mts scripts weren't updated, causing forbidNonWhitelisted ValidationPipe 400s

pnpm typecheck in CI only runs tsconfig.build.json (excludes test files) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files are never typechecked in CI even though the base tsconfig.json includes them, creating unnoticed test-file type drift (vitest v2→v3 Mock generics migration left ~50+ errors across packages)

Phase 70.1 collapsed two IndexedDB stores (generation-high-water, seq-high-water) into a single rotation-floor store (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2, keyed by nodeId) — old store names are gone entirely post-migration
cargo check for the winfsp feature fails on macOS due to windows-future dependency not compiling — expected/known limitation, Windows CI is authoritative for that feature
fuser/vendored crate produces pre-existing rustfmt warnings unrelated to any given change; verify diffs are isolated before trusting fmt output
GSD executor subagents can't read .env in their sandbox, so live sdk-e2e tests requiring secrets must be deferred to phase-verification time where the orchestrator has .env access

GSD hook fragment JSON (plan:pre capabilities) contains raw/control characters inside string values that break standard JSON.parse and even `--raw` CLI output — requires a lenient custom parser or hand-authoring the equivalent prompt

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish gated only by 'inode cid empty', so a dropped/stale UploadComplete replay would re-seal at seq=1 with a new CID and get rejected by Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate; fixed by resolving IPNS via resolve_ipns_for_replay first and routing Found outcomes into the existing CAS bump path instead of unconditional first-publish

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile P2 fix) so callers with an already-resolved sequence (the Found path in content_ops.rs) skip a redundant second resolve round-trip; the conflict-retry path always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value goes stale after a conflict

6.6.2 restore-version test used a no-op wait (detailsDialog version count===1, true both before and after a restore swap) providing zero synchronization before reading editor content, racing the restore's IPNS republish; fixed with expect.poll re-opening the editor until content matches

getWriteBodyParams (and its bin/index.ts twin) previously returned an empty write-body on any IPNS resolve miss; now distinguishes a genuine transient miss with a real (non-zero, 32-byte) writeKey present — which throws — from the legitimate zero-writeKey read-only fallback, which still succeeds silently

workflow: When multiple background CI/test runs are needed sequentially, set up a completion watcher/notification rather than polling manually — task-notifications fire automatically and let the agent continue other work

For local reproduction of CI-gated timeout-sensitive test suites, prefer running under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (e.g. temporarily patch webServer.reuseExistingServer to always-reuse and set CI=1) rather than chasing individually-tight local timeouts one flake at a time — whack-a-mole fixing under a stricter-than-CI local regime wastes many run cycles

Capture newly-discovered but out-of-scope work as a durable todo file immediately (not just a mental note) so it survives context compaction, then sequence it as a final phase plan rather than interrupting in-flight work

When a plan-checker or verifier flags only cosmetic/doc-sync warnings with no correctness impact, it's reasonable to proceed under an explicit user autonomous-execution directive rather than spend cycles fixing cosmetics

Rebase a stale feature branch onto main before dispatching a validation CI run if main has since merged commits the branch's code depends on (e.g. desktop job needs #601's FUSE fix) — otherwise the dispatch tests an incoherent state
After a squash-merge, an old planning branch with no unique commits can simply be fast-forwarded to main rather than rebased/recreated

friction: Repeated local Playwright full-workflow runs cascaded through a chain of different flaky early tests (4.10 batch delete, 4.11 batch move, 2.1 create-folder) each with its own too-tight local (non-CI-floored) timeout, blocking verification of the actual target fixes (6.6.2, 8.2) across 6+ run cycles before switching to a CI-equivalent local regime
gh workflow run -f ref= failed with HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs' because main's workflow definition predated that input — required discovering --ref as the workaround
Initial agent misread the todo directory structure (checked empty resolved/ instead of completed/), requiring a user correction mid-turn

GSD hook fragment JSON has raw control characters embedded in string values that break both JSON.parse and the CLI's --raw parsing, requiring a custom lenient parser to extract planner-contribution fragments (tdd, schema-gate, pattern-mapper)
git commit hung for ~2 minutes during lint-staged due to a suspected 1Password SSH signing prompt hang; had to verify out-of-band whether the commit actually landed before retrying
Contradictory git cat-file checks temporarily suggested the todo completed/ counterparts were missing from HEAD when they were actually present — required a second, more decisive verification pass
AskUserQuestion was interrupted/misfired once, requiring the user to clarify what needed clarifying before the assistant could re-ask a sharper question
GSD worktree execution mode risks pnpm-monorepo node_modules-missing failures in fresh worktrees, forcing a deliberate fallback to sequential main-tree execution for Phase 72
